---
title: "One day – the immigration-and-trust case"
subtitle: "Four parts of ninety minutes, with a facilitator"
---
The [case study](../../cases/trust/index.qmd), which presents the original study, the SCORE reproductions and replications and the five Multi100 reanalyses on which the day is built, is the place to start.

This is the one-day course on the immigration-and-trust case. It brings the three strands of the course together, the computational tools, the statistics and the practices of open research, on a survey study that asked, from more than a hundred thousand respondents of the European Social Survey in sixteen countries, whether citizens who see immigration as a threat to the national community trust their national politics less. Across the day you work as analyst no. 6 on a claim of the original author (OA) that five analysts reanalysed for Multi100. You reproduce the value that Multi100 recorded for one of them, write the estimand statement behind the claim, finish a causal graph that asks what each control of the paper is, work through a menu of defensible analyses, and then declare one of them in a shortened preregistration template before you run it. What you leave with is a report of your own, two marks on the class chart, one explored and one declared, and the place of your result among the 192 specifications on the curve of the claim.

The day runs as four parts of ninety minutes, with breaks of thirty, sixty and thirty minutes between them. Several of its steps are things that the class does together, such as everyone typing the *t* statistic they have just reproduced and holding it back until the facilitator says go, so the day needs a facilitator. Some stretches of the slides are optional, a short tour of the toolchain and of R in the morning and a closer look at the statistics in the afternoon, and the facilitator switches them on or off to suit the class.

| | What happens | Length |
|---|---|---|
| [Before the day](before.qmd) | Install R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), download the workspace and the file of Task 3, read the case study. | 1 to 2 hours, once |
| [Part 1 – Credibility and tools](part-1.qmd) | What a claim is for, why the field talks of a crisis, the evidence on reproduction, robustness and replication, and the toolchain; then you get running. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 2 – The claim, its estimand and its causal graph](part-2.qmd) | The paper and the five analysts, estimands and the causal-graph crash course; you write the estimand statement and finish the graph, which asks what the controls of the paper are. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 3 – Reproduction and exploration](part-3.qmd) | You reproduce the recorded result from the file of the analysts, find out what it depends on, then work the specification menu and put an exploratory mark on the class chart. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 4 – Multiverse, inference and preregistration](part-4.qmd) | The class reads its chart against the curve of 192, asks how sure sixteen countries can make anyone, meets the two replications on later rounds of the survey, and each participant declares one analysis, runs it and reports it. | 90 minutes |
| [After the day](after.qmd) | Where to go next in the companion curriculum. | as you like |
